title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold their first three-way meeting at the APEC summit in Shenzhen
seoTitle: Trump, Xi, Putin Shenzhen meeting: what is on the table
dek: The three leaders are due to meet on 19 November on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China. The White House says Trump will raise cutting nuclear weapons; Putin wants to talk about the war in Ukraine; analysts expect symbolism more than deals.
happened: Vladimir Putin proposed a three-way meeting in an October phone call with Donald Trump, and the White House confirmed on 13 November that Trump, Xi Jinping and Putin would hold talks on 19 November on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen. It would be the first such trilateral meeting. Trump is also expected to meet Xi for the third time this year, after visits to Beijing in May and the White House in September. A US-China trade truce agreed in Busan in October 2025 runs to 10 January 2027; at the peak of the trade war US tariffs on Chinese goods reached 145% and China's 125%. US imports of Chinese rare earths remain about 75% below their level before China's restrictions, according to the think tank CSIS.

sides.says: Spokeswoman Olivia Wales said Trump "will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world"; Trump said in October: "I'd love to denuclearize if possible." The White House says the US and China agreed to build a "constructive relationship of strategic stability" and will support each other at APEC and at the G20 in Florida in December.
Putin's foreign-policy adviser Yury Ushakov said the meetings' "significance and symbolism" are "hard to overestimate". Putin wants to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, RFE/RL reports.

No Chinese official is quoted in the reports read here. RFE/RL reports, through analysts, that China has resisted three-way arms-control talks, saying Russia and the US should first cut their much larger arsenals, and that German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier says Xi told him any Ukraine negotiations must include Europe.
President Zelensky told CNN: "We don't want to have Yalta 2.0."

Ali Wyne of the Crisis Group said Trump "will work to strengthen his rapport with Xi, but the meeting is unlikely to produce any substantive breakthroughs". Yun Sun of the Stimson Center said Xi's priority is "a successful gathering", and Hudson Institute's Tsiporah Fried said Putin stands to gain the most even if the summit achieves little.

next: The trilateral meeting is scheduled for 19 November in Shenzhen. RFE/RL, citing the Wall Street Journal, reports that Beijing wants a tightly scripted meeting with an agreed outcome while Washington prefers a looser format. This page will be updated after the meeting.
summary: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are due to hold their first three-way meeting on 19 November at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. The White House says Trump will raise cutting nuclear weapons, Russia wants to discuss Ukraine, and China has resisted three-way arms talks. Trade, tariffs and rare earths are also in the background of a separate Trump-Xi meeting. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera and RFE/RL expect symbolism rather than breakthroughs.
